phases.name: Research Foundations & Lab Onboarding
phases.theme: scientific computing, problem formulation, literature search & applied statistics
phases.purpose: Become a reliable contributor who can enter a lab, find a gap, and make defensible claims.

phases.name: Data Curation & Modeling Paradigms
phases.theme: domain datasets, classical ML, deep learning, computer vision, graphs and sequence models
phases.purpose: Turn real-world data and model architectures into testable research baselines.

phases.name: Generative Models & Experimental Science
phases.theme: generative modeling, controlled ablations, fair benchmarks and scaled experimental systems
phases.purpose: Design controlled experiments and scale them far enough to reveal meaningful behavior.

phases.name: Scaled Systems, Trustworthy AI & Alignment
phases.theme: foundation models, interpretability, robustness, fairness and alignment for high-impact domains
phases.purpose: Study powerful models critically and evaluate their behavior, risks, and limits.

phases.name: Cross-Disciplinary Research & Capstones
phases.theme: multimodal methods and thesis-grade projects that turn questions into defensible evidence
phases.purpose: Lead a complete, cross-disciplinary research project from question to evidence.

phases.name: Publishing, Thesis Defense & Research Careers
phases.theme: manuscripts, peer review, rebuttals, thesis defense, job talks and research scientist pathways
phases.purpose: Communicate, defend, publish, and carry research into academic or industrial employment.

levels.title: Computing, Python & Learning Habits
levels.scope: Build the everyday computing, Python, communication, and study habits needed to learn data science without relying on copy-paste tutorials.
levels.prereqStated: None; designed for a complete beginner

modules.name: Computer and Command-Line Foundations

objectives.text: Explain how files, folders, programs, memory, and networks work together.
Navigate a terminal, create files, inspect processes, and read error messages.
Use a Linux shell, SSH, environment variables, and a remote notebook safely.
Organize research notes, downloads, datasets, and code with predictable names.
Protect credentials, recognize unsafe commands, and keep private data out of repositories.
Describe licenses, attribution, accessibility, and responsible use of AI tools.

modules.mentalModel: The command line is a precise laboratory instrument, not a mysterious black box.
modules.tryIt: Create a small project folder, document every command in a lab notebook, and reproduce the setup on a second machine.
modules.outcome: You can work safely in a computing environment and explain what your tools are doing.
modules.evidence: Create a small project folder, document every command in a lab notebook, and reproduce the setup on a second machine.

modules.name: Python Programming for Data Work

objectives.text: Use variables, strings, numbers, booleans, conditionals, loops, and functions.
Break a task into small functions and test each function with simple examples.
Work with lists, dictionaries, sets, tuples, CSV files, and JSON documents.
Handle missing files and malformed input with clear, user-facing errors.
Import standard-library modules, read tracebacks, and debug with a small reproducible example.
Use type hints and docstrings to make beginner code understandable to collaborators.
Write a script that loads a dataset, computes summary statistics, and saves a report.
Run the same script from a clean terminal and record its inputs and outputs.

modules.mentalModel: Programming is the practice of turning an explicit procedure into repeatable instructions.
modules.tryIt: Build a command-line dataset summary tool with tests for empty, missing, and malformed inputs.
modules.outcome: You can write, run, debug, and explain small Python programs for data tasks.
modules.evidence: Build a command-line dataset summary tool with tests for empty, missing, and malformed inputs.

modules.name: Git, Documentation & Deliberate Learning

objectives.text: Initialize a Git repository, make focused commits, inspect diffs, and recover from mistakes.
Use branches and pull requests to ask for review without losing working code.
Write a README with purpose, setup, usage, limitations, and an example result.
Turn a confusing error or experiment into a concise issue containing evidence and a question.
Plan weekly study blocks, use retrieval practice, and maintain a questions-and-evidence log.
Distinguish understanding a concept from recognizing a familiar code pattern.

modules.mentalModel: A research career compounds small, documented improvements rather than isolated bursts of motivation.
modules.tryIt: Publish a beginner-friendly repository with a README, changelog, issue, and three meaningful commits.
modules.outcome: You can learn in public, collaborate with version control, and communicate technical work clearly.
modules.evidence: Publish a beginner-friendly repository with a README, changelog, issue, and three meaningful commits.

modules.name: Capstone: Reproducible Beginner Data Project

objectives.text: Choose a small open dataset and state one descriptive question without claiming causation.
Build a Python analysis with a clean README, requirements file, validation checks, and a results table.
Add a short reflection describing what changed between the first and final version.

modules.finalResult: A public, reproducible repository demonstrating safe computing, beginner Python, Git, documentation, and honest interpretation.
modules.evidence: A public, reproducible repository demonstrating safe computing, beginner Python, Git, documentation, and honest interpretation.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can learn, code, and communicate without copying blindly.
completionOutcomes: You can work safely in a computing environment and explain what your tools are doing.
You can write, run, debug, and explain small Python programs for data tasks.
You can learn in public, collaborate with version control, and communicate technical work clearly.
A public, reproducible repository demonstrating safe computing, beginner Python, Git, documentation, and honest interpretation.

levels.title: Mathematics for Data Science
levels.scope: Develop the algebra, functions, calculus, and linear algebra intuition required to understand models instead of treating libraries as magic.

modules.name: Algebra, Functions & Logarithms

objectives.text: Manipulate equations, ratios, inequalities, powers, logarithms, and summations.
Read a function as an input-output rule and interpret slope, curvature, and scale.
Use units, orders of magnitude, and dimensional checks to catch impossible results.

modules.mentalModel: Mathematical notation is a compact language for describing relationships that code can execute.
modules.tryIt: Implement and plot linear, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions, then explain where each is useful.
modules.outcome: You can translate common quantitative statements between words, equations, plots, and Python.
modules.evidence: Implement and plot linear, polynomial, exponential, and logarithmic functions, then explain where each is useful.

modules.name: Linear Algebra & Geometry

objectives.text: Represent vectors, matrices, tensors, basis changes, dot products, norms, and projections.
Derive matrix multiplication dimensions and use geometric language to explain distance and similarity.
Implement a small neural layer with NumPy and verify it against hand-calculated examples.

modules.mentalModel: Most machine-learning computation is geometry performed efficiently on batches of examples.
modules.tryIt: Build a visual notebook for projections, least squares, principal components, and cosine similarity.
modules.outcome: You can follow the linear-algebra operations behind regression, embeddings, and neural networks.
modules.evidence: Build a visual notebook for projections, least squares, principal components, and cosine similarity.

modules.name: Derivatives and Optimization Intuition

objectives.text: Interpret derivatives, partial derivatives, gradients, Jacobians, and Hessians.
Apply the chain rule to a small computation graph and check gradients numerically.
Explain learning rate, local minima, conditioning, and why normalization affects optimization.

modules.mentalModel: Training adjusts parameters in directions that reduce a chosen error surface.
modules.tryIt: Implement gradient descent for a one-variable and two-variable function and compare step sizes.
modules.outcome: You can explain and verify the calculus used to train predictive models.
modules.evidence: Implement gradient descent for a one-variable and two-variable function and compare step sizes.

modules.name: Capstone: Mathematical Model Notebook

objectives.text: Derive ordinary least squares from a clearly stated objective and assumptions.
Implement the solution with NumPy and compare it with a trusted library.
Include plots, dimensional checks, numerical-gradient checks, and a plain-language explanation.

modules.finalResult: A mathematical notebook that connects equations, geometry, optimization, code, and model behavior.
modules.evidence: A mathematical notebook that connects equations, geometry, optimization, code, and model behavior.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can explain the quantitative foundations of model behavior.
completionOutcomes: You can translate common quantitative statements between words, equations, plots, and Python.
You can follow the linear-algebra operations behind regression, embeddings, and neural networks.
You can explain and verify the calculus used to train predictive models.
A mathematical notebook that connects equations, geometry, optimization, code, and model behavior.

levels.title: Probability, Statistics & Uncertainty
levels.scope: Learn to describe variation, estimate uncertainty, and distinguish a useful pattern from an accidental result.

modules.name: Probability and Random Variables

objectives.text: Work with events, conditional probability, independence, Bayes' rule, and random variables.
Interpret expectation, variance, covariance, common distributions, and sampling.
Simulate probability experiments and compare empirical frequencies with theoretical values.

modules.mentalModel: Probability is a language for reasoning when observations and outcomes are uncertain.
modules.tryIt: Simulate a clinical screening example and show how base rates change the meaning of a positive test.
modules.outcome: You can model uncertainty and explain conditional reasoning without relying on slogans.
modules.evidence: Simulate a clinical screening example and show how base rates change the meaning of a positive test.

modules.name: Estimation, Intervals & Hypothesis Tests

objectives.text: Construct point estimates, bootstrap intervals, confidence intervals, and practical effect sizes.
State null and alternative hypotheses, choose a test, and report assumptions and limitations.
Separate statistical significance, practical importance, and the number of comparisons being made.

modules.mentalModel: An estimate without uncertainty is an incomplete scientific claim.
modules.tryIt: Bootstrap the difference in two model accuracies and write a result paragraph with an interval.
modules.outcome: You can quantify uncertainty and report statistical comparisons responsibly.
modules.evidence: Bootstrap the difference in two model accuracies and write a result paragraph with an interval.

modules.name: Experimental Data Analysis

objectives.text: Use pandas and visualization to inspect distributions, missingness, outliers, and subgroup differences.
Detect selection bias, confounding, leakage, survivorship bias, and Simpson's paradox.
Choose train, validation, and test splits before looking at test outcomes.

modules.mentalModel: Analysis decisions are part of the experiment and must be recorded before results are known.
modules.tryIt: Audit a public dataset, create a data-quality report, and list threats to validity before modeling.
modules.outcome: You can turn raw observations into a defensible exploratory and statistical analysis.
modules.evidence: Audit a public dataset, create a data-quality report, and list threats to validity before modeling.

modules.name: Capstone: Uncertainty and Bias Audit

objectives.text: Select a public dataset and define a population, sampling process, outcome, and estimand.
Produce an exploratory report with uncertainty intervals, subgroup checks, and a pre-analysis plan.
Explain which conclusions are supported, which are tentative, and which cannot be made.

modules.finalResult: A transparent statistical audit that demonstrates scientific caution, reproducible analysis, and honest limits.
modules.evidence: A transparent statistical audit that demonstrates scientific caution, reproducible analysis, and honest limits.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can interpret data without overstating what it proves.
completionOutcomes: You can model uncertainty and explain conditional reasoning without relying on slogans.
You can quantify uncertainty and report statistical comparisons responsibly.
You can turn raw observations into a defensible exploratory and statistical analysis.
A transparent statistical audit that demonstrates scientific caution, reproducible analysis, and honest limits.

levels.title: Research Literacy and Problem Formulation
levels.scope: Learn how research questions are discovered, evaluated, scoped, and communicated before a model is selected.

modules.name: Finding and Reading Research Papers

objectives.text: Search scholarly databases, follow citation graphs, and record inclusion and exclusion decisions.
Read papers in passes: claim and structure, method and evidence, then limitations and reproduction details.
Maintain a literature matrix containing question, data, method, comparison, result, and unresolved issue.

modules.mentalModel: A paper is an argument supported by evidence, not a list of fashionable techniques.
modules.tryIt: Read five papers on one question and create a one-page evidence map with disagreements.
modules.outcome: You can find relevant literature and explain what a paper actually establishes.
modules.evidence: Read five papers on one question and create a one-page evidence map with disagreements.

modules.name: Questions, Hypotheses & Research Designs

objectives.text: Turn a broad interest into a specific, measurable, falsifiable research question.
Define variables, estimands, baselines, success criteria, and plausible alternative explanations.
Match exploratory, observational, experimental, and qualitative designs to the question.

modules.mentalModel: Good research narrows uncertainty by making competing explanations testable.
modules.tryIt: Convert an interesting model idea into three hypotheses and a preregistered experiment outline.
modules.outcome: You can formulate research questions that are feasible, meaningful, and testable.
modules.evidence: Convert an interesting model idea into three hypotheses and a preregistered experiment outline.

modules.name: Reproducibility, Ethics & Collaboration

objectives.text: Use research logs, data statements, code review, preregistration, and artifact checklists.
Explain informed consent, privacy, intellectual property, authorship, conflicts of interest, and dual use.
Give and receive feedback using a claim-evidence-limitation structure.

modules.mentalModel: Trust is an engineering property built through transparent choices and accountable collaboration.
modules.tryIt: Review a peer's project proposal and request evidence for every major claim.
modules.outcome: You can participate in a research group with ethical judgment and reproducible habits.
modules.evidence: Review a peer's project proposal and request evidence for every major claim.

modules.name: Capstone: Literature Review and Research Proposal

objectives.text: Select a tractable data-science question and synthesize at least ten relevant sources.
Write a proposal containing motivation, gap, hypotheses, data plan, methods, evaluation, risks, and timeline.
Defend the proposal in a short presentation and revise it from recorded feedback.

modules.finalResult: A research proposal that turns a beginner's interest into a feasible, evidence-aware study.
modules.evidence: A research proposal that turns a beginner's interest into a feasible, evidence-aware study.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can turn an interest into a feasible, testable study.
completionOutcomes: You can find relevant literature and explain what a paper actually establishes.
You can formulate research questions that are feasible, meaningful, and testable.
You can participate in a research group with ethical judgment and reproducible habits.
A research proposal that turns a beginner's interest into a feasible, evidence-aware study.

levels.title: Data Collection, SQL & Data Stewardship
levels.scope: Build reliable datasets from messy sources while preserving provenance, privacy, meaning, and the ability to audit every transformation.

modules.name: SQL, APIs & Data Acquisition

objectives.text: Query relational data with SELECT, JOIN, GROUP BY, window functions, and common table expressions.
Retrieve data from documented APIs with pagination, retries, rate limits, and schema validation.
Record source, access date, version, license, and transformation history for every input.

modules.mentalModel: A dataset is a claim about the world plus a chain of decisions that produced it.
modules.tryIt: Build a small ingestion job that loads API data into SQLite with validation and provenance logs.
modules.outcome: You can acquire structured data reproducibly and query it to answer precise questions.
modules.evidence: Build a small ingestion job that loads API data into SQLite with validation and provenance logs.

modules.name: Cleaning, Labels & Data Quality

objectives.text: Diagnose missing values, duplicates, inconsistent units, outliers, label noise, and schema drift.
Design annotation guidelines, adjudication workflows, and inter-rater agreement checks.
Prevent train-test leakage during preprocessing, deduplication, feature selection, and augmentation.

modules.mentalModel: Cleaning changes the measurement process, so every cleaning rule is a research decision.
modules.tryIt: Create a data-quality dashboard and a label handbook for a small supervised-learning dataset.
modules.outcome: You can make a dataset model-ready without hiding uncertainty or silently changing its meaning.
modules.evidence: Create a data-quality dashboard and a label handbook for a small supervised-learning dataset.

modules.name: Privacy, Governance & Dataset Documentation

objectives.text: Apply data minimization, de-identification, access control, retention, and secure storage principles.
Write a datasheet describing motivation, composition, collection, preprocessing, uses, risks, and limitations.
Explain when consent, review, licensing, or domain expertise is required before analysis.

modules.mentalModel: Useful data is not automatically permissible data.
modules.tryIt: Complete a data card and risk register before downloading or sharing a sensitive dataset.
modules.outcome: You can steward data responsibly and explain who may use it, how, and under which limits.
modules.evidence: Complete a data card and risk register before downloading or sharing a sensitive dataset.

modules.name: Capstone: Auditable Dataset and Benchmark Pipeline

objectives.text: Acquire a public dataset, version its raw and processed forms, and define a leakage-safe split.
Implement validation checks, a dataset card, a feature dictionary, and a reproducible benchmark loader.
Publish a small sample and an audit report rather than exposing restricted records.

modules.finalResult: A documented, governed, queryable dataset pipeline ready for honest modeling experiments.
modules.evidence: A documented, governed, queryable dataset pipeline ready for honest modeling experiments.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can turn messy data into governed evidence.
completionOutcomes: You can acquire structured data reproducibly and query it to answer precise questions.
You can make a dataset model-ready without hiding uncertainty or silently changing its meaning.
You can steward data responsibly and explain who may use it, how, and under which limits.
A documented, governed, queryable dataset pipeline ready for honest modeling experiments.

levels.title: Classical Machine Learning and Baselines
levels.scope: Learn the supervised, unsupervised, and time-aware modeling families that form the baseline for nearly every applied data-science investigation.

modules.name: Regression, Classification & Feature Design

objectives.text: Fit and interpret linear models, logistic regression, regularized models, trees, and gradient boosting.
Design features from domain meaning while separating training-only transformations from evaluation data.
Compare calibration, discrimination, ranking, and error costs instead of relying on accuracy alone.

modules.mentalModel: A baseline is a scientific control that tells you whether complexity is buying useful signal.
modules.tryIt: Build a leakage-safe scikit-learn pipeline and compare a linear model, random forest, and gradient booster.
modules.outcome: You can establish strong, interpretable baselines for structured prediction problems.
modules.evidence: Build a leakage-safe scikit-learn pipeline and compare a linear model, random forest, and gradient booster.

modules.name: Unsupervised Learning and Representation

objectives.text: Use clustering, dimensionality reduction, anomaly detection, and similarity search appropriately.
Compare stability and usefulness of discovered groups across seeds, samples, and feature choices.
Explain why visualization is exploratory evidence rather than proof of a natural cluster.

modules.mentalModel: Unsupervised outputs are hypotheses about structure that require validation.
modules.tryIt: Cluster a dataset, test cluster stability, and interview the domain meaning of the resulting groups.
modules.outcome: You can use unsupervised tools without overinterpreting attractive plots.
modules.evidence: Cluster a dataset, test cluster stability, and interview the domain meaning of the resulting groups.

modules.name: Model Selection and Error Analysis

objectives.text: Use cross-validation, nested selection, learning curves, hyperparameter search, and calibration.
Create an error taxonomy and inspect representative false positives, false negatives, and edge cases.
Compare models with confidence intervals and subgroup metrics tied to the deployment question.

modules.mentalModel: Model development is an investigation of failure, not a leaderboard chase.
modules.tryIt: Produce an error-analysis report that changes one modeling decision based on observed failures.
modules.outcome: You can select models using evidence, constraints, and failure analysis.
modules.evidence: Produce an error-analysis report that changes one modeling decision based on observed failures.

modules.name: Capstone: Reproducible Baseline Study

objectives.text: Reproduce a classical ML result on an open dataset with an explicit split and pre-analysis plan.
Compare at least three model families, report uncertainty, calibration, cost-sensitive metrics, and failures.
Package the code, configuration, data statement, and results table for another person to rerun.

modules.finalResult: A baseline paper-style report proving that you can make a credible first claim before using deep learning.
modules.evidence: A baseline paper-style report proving that you can make a credible first claim before using deep learning.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can choose simple models and establish a credible control.
completionOutcomes: You can establish strong, interpretable baselines for structured prediction problems.
You can use unsupervised tools without overinterpreting attractive plots.
You can select models using evidence, constraints, and failure analysis.
A baseline paper-style report proving that you can make a credible first claim before using deep learning.

levels.title: Deep Learning Foundations
levels.scope: Understand neural networks from tensor operations through training, regularization, debugging, and responsible use of pretrained models.

modules.name: Neural Networks and Automatic Differentiation

objectives.text: Implement affine layers, activations, losses, backpropagation, and minibatch training.
Trace tensor shapes, device placement, gradients, and parameter updates in PyTorch.
Explain initialization, normalization, dropout, weight decay, and overfitting.

modules.mentalModel: A neural network is a parameterized function whose behavior is learned through repeated error signals.
modules.tryIt: Implement a small multilayer perceptron twice: once with NumPy gradients and once with PyTorch autograd.
modules.outcome: You can inspect and debug the complete training loop of a neural network.
modules.evidence: Implement a small multilayer perceptron twice: once with NumPy gradients and once with PyTorch autograd.

modules.name: Computer Vision and Convolutional Models

objectives.text: Explain convolution, receptive fields, pooling, augmentation, residual connections, and transfer learning.
Build image classification and segmentation pipelines with correct spatial transforms and evaluation.
Inspect saliency and failure cases without treating visual explanations as causal proof.

modules.mentalModel: Convolutions encode local structure, while data and labels determine what the model learns.
modules.tryIt: Compare a scratch CNN and a pretrained backbone on a small image dataset with a documented error taxonomy.
modules.outcome: You can build and evaluate reproducible computer-vision baselines.
modules.evidence: Compare a scratch CNN and a pretrained backbone on a small image dataset with a documented error taxonomy.

modules.name: Training Engineering and Debugging

objectives.text: Use learning-rate schedules, mixed precision, gradient clipping, checkpoint recovery, and early stopping.
Detect underfitting, overfitting, data bugs, unstable loss, and silent label or preprocessing errors.
Profile memory and throughput so training choices are tied to measured bottlenecks.

modules.mentalModel: Most failed experiments are diagnosed by checking data, shapes, targets, and instrumentation before changing architecture.
modules.tryIt: Intentionally introduce three training bugs, diagnose them from logs, and document the fixes.
modules.outcome: You can run reliable neural-network experiments and explain why a training run succeeded or failed.
modules.evidence: Intentionally introduce three training bugs, diagnose them from logs, and document the fixes.

modules.name: Capstone: Deep Learning Reproduction

objectives.text: Reimplement a published neural baseline from its paper and public code.
Match its data split, preprocessing, metric, training budget, and reported uncertainty as closely as possible.
Explain every mismatch and propose one follow-up experiment that would meaningfully test the method.

modules.finalResult: A reproducibility report demonstrating implementation skill, scientific skepticism, and transparent comparison.
modules.evidence: A reproducibility report demonstrating implementation skill, scientific skepticism, and transparent comparison.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can implement, debug, and reproduce a neural method.
completionOutcomes: You can inspect and debug the complete training loop of a neural network.
You can build and evaluate reproducible computer-vision baselines.
You can run reliable neural-network experiments and explain why a training run succeeded or failed.
A reproducibility report demonstrating implementation skill, scientific skepticism, and transparent comparison.

levels.title: Modern Architectures: Sequences, Graphs and Transformers
levels.scope: Select and adapt architectures for language, time series, relational data, and long-context problems while connecting design choices to inductive bias.

modules.name: Sequences, Time Series & Attention

objectives.text: Represent sequences with windows, masks, positional information, recurrence, convolution, and attention.
Forecast or classify time-dependent data using time-aware splits and horizon-specific metrics.
Identify temporal leakage caused by random splits, future features, and duplicated entities.

modules.mentalModel: A sequence model should only use information that would have existed at prediction time.
modules.tryIt: Compare a persistence baseline, recurrent model, temporal convolution, and attention model on one forecasting task.
modules.outcome: You can design honest experiments for sequential and time-dependent data.
modules.evidence: Compare a persistence baseline, recurrent model, temporal convolution, and attention model on one forecasting task.

modules.name: Transformers and Language Modeling

objectives.text: Explain tokenization, embeddings, self-attention, masking, positional information, and next-token prediction.
Implement a small transformer and inspect attention, loss, context length, and scaling behavior.
Evaluate language models with task metrics, calibration, qualitative error analysis, and contamination awareness.

modules.mentalModel: Attention is content-dependent information routing, not an automatic explanation of reasoning.
modules.tryIt: Train a tiny language model on a permitted corpus and write a report on data, objective, and limitations.
modules.outcome: You can implement and reason about the core transformer training loop.
modules.evidence: Train a tiny language model on a permitted corpus and write a report on data, objective, and limitations.

modules.name: Graph Learning and Architecture Choice

objectives.text: Represent nodes, edges, attributes, graph splits, message passing, and inductive versus transductive settings.
Compare graph convolution, graph attention, and simple non-graph baselines.
Choose an architecture by data structure and scientific question rather than novelty alone.

modules.mentalModel: An architecture is a prior about which relationships should influence a prediction.
modules.tryIt: Build a graph benchmark with a leakage-safe edge or node split and compare it to feature-only models.
modules.outcome: You can adapt modern architectures to relational and structured data.
modules.evidence: Build a graph benchmark with a leakage-safe edge or node split and compare it to feature-only models.

modules.name: Capstone: Architecture Selection Study

objectives.text: Define one task that can be represented as tabular, sequential, or relational data.
Compare appropriate model families under matched data, compute, and tuning budgets.
Connect each performance difference to an inductive bias, failure mode, or data property.

modules.finalResult: A comparative study that demonstrates architecture reasoning instead of architecture collecting.
modules.evidence: A comparative study that demonstrates architecture reasoning instead of architecture collecting.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can connect model design to data structure and evidence.
completionOutcomes: You can design honest experiments for sequential and time-dependent data.
You can implement and reason about the core transformer training loop.
You can adapt modern architectures to relational and structured data.
A comparative study that demonstrates architecture reasoning instead of architecture collecting.

levels.title: Experimental Design, Evaluation & Causal Reasoning
levels.scope: Turn model ideas into experiments whose comparisons, metrics, uncertainty, and limitations can withstand skeptical review.

modules.name: Measurement and Evaluation Design

objectives.text: Define the construct being measured and select metrics that reflect the real decision or scientific claim.
Build baselines, holdout sets, challenge sets, and subgroup slices before tuning on results.
Report confidence intervals, calibration, ranking uncertainty, and clinically or operationally meaningful thresholds.

modules.mentalModel: A metric is an instrument; its reading is only useful when its validity and failure modes are understood.
modules.tryIt: Replace a single accuracy score with an evaluation plan that measures utility, harm, calibration, and subgroup behavior.
modules.outcome: You can design evaluation protocols that measure the claim rather than a convenient proxy.
modules.evidence: Replace a single accuracy score with an evaluation plan that measures utility, harm, calibration, and subgroup behavior.

modules.name: Ablations, Sensitivity and Compute Matching

objectives.text: Isolate components with controlled ablations, matched budgets, seed repeats, and sensitivity analyses.
Separate tuning data from final evidence and report unsuccessful configurations.
Use experiment registries and configuration files to make every comparison auditable.

modules.mentalModel: A contribution is credible only when its claimed cause is isolated from confounding changes.
modules.tryIt: Reproduce a headline result with an ablation matrix and identify which component actually matters.
modules.outcome: You can distinguish a real contribution from tuning luck or an unfair comparison.
modules.evidence: Reproduce a headline result with an ablation matrix and identify which component actually matters.

modules.name: Causal Thinking and External Validity

objectives.text: Draw causal diagrams and identify confounders, mediators, selection effects, and interventions.
Distinguish prediction, association, and causal effect claims in model reports.
Test robustness across sites, time periods, populations, and plausible distribution shifts.

modules.mentalModel: Better prediction does not automatically explain why an outcome happens or what an intervention will change.
modules.tryIt: Write a causal diagram for a deployed prediction system and list the assumptions needed for each claim.
modules.outcome: You can state what an experiment identifies and where its conclusions may not transfer.
modules.evidence: Write a causal diagram for a deployed prediction system and list the assumptions needed for each claim.

modules.name: Capstone: Peer-Review-Ready Benchmark

objectives.text: Build a benchmark suite with preregistered hypotheses, strong baselines, ablations, repeated seeds, and error analysis.
Include compute, data, metric, and limitation disclosures.
Have a peer review the protocol before running the final experiments and record all changes.

modules.finalResult: A fair, auditable evaluation package suitable for the results section of a research paper.
modules.evidence: A fair, auditable evaluation package suitable for the results section of a research paper.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can isolate contributions and state causal limits.
completionOutcomes: You can design evaluation protocols that measure the claim rather than a convenient proxy.
You can distinguish a real contribution from tuning luck or an unfair comparison.
You can state what an experiment identifies and where its conclusions may not transfer.
A fair, auditable evaluation package suitable for the results section of a research paper.

levels.title: Generative Models and Foundation-Model Use
levels.scope: Understand how generative models are trained, evaluated, adapted, and used responsibly for research rather than treating generated text or images as evidence.

modules.name: Generative Modeling Principles

objectives.text: Explain autoregressive, variational, energy-based, diffusion, and flow-matching perspectives.
Implement a small generative model and inspect likelihood, sampling, conditioning, and failure modes.
Compare fidelity, diversity, calibration, utility, and memorization rather than relying on visual appeal.

modules.mentalModel: Generation learns a distribution; a convincing sample does not prove coverage, truth, or usefulness.
modules.tryIt: Train a toy diffusion or flow model and evaluate samples with quantitative and qualitative checks.
modules.outcome: You can explain and evaluate the basic families of generative models.
modules.evidence: Train a toy diffusion or flow model and evaluate samples with quantitative and qualitative checks.

modules.name: Pretrained Models, Prompting and Retrieval

objectives.text: Use model cards, tokenizers, prompts, structured outputs, retrieval, citations, and abstention patterns.
Evaluate factuality, robustness, contamination, and sensitivity to prompts and context.
Keep retrieved evidence separate from model-generated claims in an analysis pipeline.

modules.mentalModel: A foundation model is a probabilistic component whose outputs require measurement and provenance.
modules.tryIt: Build a small retrieval-augmented experiment with a citation checker and an abstention test set.
modules.outcome: You can use pretrained models as research instruments without confusing fluency with truth.
modules.evidence: Build a small retrieval-augmented experiment with a citation checker and an abstention test set.

modules.name: Adaptation and Efficiency

objectives.text: Compare zero-shot, few-shot, supervised fine-tuning, adapters, LoRA, and prompt-based adaptation.
Track data provenance, trainable parameters, compute, checkpoints, and evaluation leakage.
Decide when adaptation is justified over retrieval, better data, or a simpler baseline.

modules.mentalModel: Adaptation changes a model's behavior through a data and optimization budget that must be measured.
modules.tryIt: Adapt a small open model with LoRA and compare it with retrieval and prompting under a fixed budget.
modules.outcome: You can choose and evaluate an adaptation strategy with transparent trade-offs.
modules.evidence: Adapt a small open model with LoRA and compare it with retrieval and prompting under a fixed budget.

modules.name: Capstone: Generative System Evaluation

objectives.text: Define a real use case, threat model, permitted data, and success criteria before implementation.
Compare a generative baseline, retrieval system, and adapted model with human or domain checks.
Publish prompts, evaluation examples, failure cases, costs, and known unsafe or unsupported uses.

modules.finalResult: A responsible generative-AI research report grounded in evidence rather than demos.
modules.evidence: A responsible generative-AI research report grounded in evidence rather than demos.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can evaluate foundation-model behavior beyond a demo.
completionOutcomes: You can explain and evaluate the basic families of generative models.
You can use pretrained models as research instruments without confusing fluency with truth.
You can choose and evaluate an adaptation strategy with transparent trade-offs.
A responsible generative-AI research report grounded in evidence rather than demos.

levels.title: Research Systems, MLOps and Scaling
levels.scope: Move from notebooks to reliable research systems that can run, scale, observe, and be reproduced by a team.

modules.name: Packaging, Testing and Data Pipelines

objectives.text: Package a research project with locked dependencies, configuration, unit tests, data checks, and continuous integration.
Separate exploration, reusable library code, training, evaluation, and reporting.
Make pipelines resumable, cacheable, observable, and safe to rerun.

modules.mentalModel: Research software is an instrument whose failure modes must be tested like a laboratory device.
modules.tryIt: Convert a notebook experiment into a tested command-line pipeline with one-command reproduction.
modules.outcome: You can turn exploratory code into maintainable research software.
modules.evidence: Convert a notebook experiment into a tested command-line pipeline with one-command reproduction.

modules.name: Experiment Operations and Model Serving

objectives.text: Track datasets, configurations, runs, artifacts, checkpoints, and lineage in an experiment registry.
Measure latency, throughput, memory, cost, and reliability for batch and online inference.
Add data validation, model monitoring, rollback, and incident documentation.

modules.mentalModel: A model is only useful when its behavior remains observable after it leaves the notebook.
modules.tryIt: Serve a small model behind an API and measure performance, failure responses, and resource use.
modules.outcome: You can operate a model experiment and report its engineering as well as scientific performance.
modules.evidence: Serve a small model behind an API and measure performance, failure responses, and resource use.

modules.name: GPUs, Distributed Training and Scaling Laws

objectives.text: Profile input pipelines, memory, communication, utilization, and numerical precision.
Explain data parallelism, gradient accumulation, checkpointing, and distributed failure recovery.
Design scaling experiments that vary data, parameters, compute, and context without confounding them.

modules.mentalModel: Scaling is a measured systems experiment, not simply adding more hardware.
modules.tryIt: Run a controlled single-GPU and multi-GPU comparison and publish throughput, cost, and quality curves.
modules.outcome: You can scale an experiment while preserving evidence about what changed and why.
modules.evidence: Run a controlled single-GPU and multi-GPU comparison and publish throughput, cost, and quality curves.

modules.name: Capstone: Reproducible Research Platform

objectives.text: Build a template that provisions an environment, validates data, launches a tracked run, evaluates it, and exports a report.
Add failure recovery, resource limits, tests, and documentation for a new collaborator.
Demonstrate reproduction on a second machine or clean environment.

modules.finalResult: A dependable research platform that supports collaboration, scaling, and artifact evaluation.
modules.evidence: A dependable research platform that supports collaboration, scaling, and artifact evaluation.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can run reliable experiments across people, machines, and budgets.
completionOutcomes: You can turn exploratory code into maintainable research software.
You can operate a model experiment and report its engineering as well as scientific performance.
You can scale an experiment while preserving evidence about what changed and why.
A dependable research platform that supports collaboration, scaling, and artifact evaluation.

levels.title: Interpretability, Robustness and Fairness
levels.scope: Study model behavior, failure, distribution shift, security, and social impact with methods that support actionable claims.

modules.name: Model Behavior and Interpretability

objectives.text: Compare feature attribution, counterfactuals, probing, concept methods, and mechanistic analyses.
Test explanation faithfulness, stability, usefulness, and sensitivity to baselines.
Treat an explanation as a hypothesis about computation that requires independent validation.

modules.mentalModel: An explanation is evidence about a model, not a guarantee that the model used a human-readable reason.
modules.tryIt: Evaluate two explanation methods on known synthetic mechanisms before applying them to a real model.
modules.outcome: You can make cautious, testable interpretability claims.
modules.evidence: Evaluate two explanation methods on known synthetic mechanisms before applying them to a real model.

modules.name: Robustness and Security

objectives.text: Test corruption, perturbation, distribution shift, prompt injection, data poisoning, and model extraction risks.
Define threat models, attacker capabilities, budgets, and realistic success criteria.
Compare robust training, input validation, uncertainty, monitoring, and abstention mitigations.

modules.mentalModel: Security claims are conditional statements about a specified attacker and environment.
modules.tryIt: Write a threat model and red-team protocol before testing a model; never test against systems you do not own.
modules.outcome: You can evaluate and mitigate realistic reliability and security failures.
modules.evidence: Write a threat model and red-team protocol before testing a model; never test against systems you do not own.

modules.name: Fairness, Privacy and Human Impact

objectives.text: Measure subgroup performance, calibration, allocation effects, privacy risk, and representational harms.
Explain why fairness metrics can conflict and why context and stakeholder participation matter.
Document intended use, excluded use, affected groups, recourse, and residual risk.

modules.mentalModel: Responsible AI is a design and governance process, not a single metric added after training.
modules.tryIt: Produce an impact assessment with stakeholder questions and a mitigation trade-off table.
modules.outcome: You can connect technical evaluation to human consequences and governance decisions.
modules.evidence: Produce an impact assessment with stakeholder questions and a mitigation trade-off table.

modules.name: Capstone: Trustworthy-AI Evaluation

objectives.text: Audit one model across interpretability, robustness, fairness, privacy, and documentation dimensions.
Prioritize risks by severity and likelihood, then test whether mitigations improve the stated risk.
Present unresolved risks plainly to a technical and non-technical audience.

modules.finalResult: A trustworthy-AI audit that demonstrates measurement, threat modeling, stakeholder awareness, and responsible communication.
modules.evidence: A trustworthy-AI audit that demonstrates measurement, threat modeling, stakeholder awareness, and responsible communication.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can measure model risk and communicate residual harm.
completionOutcomes: You can make cautious, testable interpretability claims.
You can evaluate and mitigate realistic reliability and security failures.
You can connect technical evaluation to human consequences and governance decisions.
A trustworthy-AI audit that demonstrates measurement, threat modeling, stakeholder awareness, and responsible communication.

levels.title: Multimodal and Domain Research
levels.scope: Translate research methods across images, text, audio, tables, and domain workflows while working with experts who understand the problem better than the model builder.

modules.name: Multimodal Representation and Fusion

objectives.text: Align image, text, audio, tabular, and temporal representations with suitable encoders and objectives.
Compare early fusion, late fusion, cross-attention, contrastive learning, and missing-modality strategies.
Evaluate whether a multimodal gain comes from useful interaction or simply additional information.

modules.mentalModel: Combining modalities is a measurement and alignment problem before it is an architecture problem.
modules.tryIt: Build a two-modality classifier with modality ablations and inspect performance when one modality is missing.
modules.outcome: You can design multimodal experiments that expose the source of a claimed improvement.
modules.evidence: Build a two-modality classifier with modality ablations and inspect performance when one modality is missing.

modules.name: Domain Adaptation and Expert Collaboration

objectives.text: Translate a domain workflow into labels, constraints, outcomes, and reviewable decision points.
Use domain interviews, annotation pilots, disagreement analysis, and expert validation.
Distinguish benchmark success from usefulness, safety, and adoption in the real workflow.

modules.mentalModel: Domain experts are research partners who define validity, not merely label providers.
modules.tryIt: Run an annotation pilot with a domain reviewer and revise the codebook from disagreements.
modules.outcome: You can conduct cross-disciplinary research without flattening domain knowledge.
modules.evidence: Run an annotation pilot with a domain reviewer and revise the codebook from disagreements.

modules.name: Applied Research and Deployment Evidence

objectives.text: Design prospective, retrospective, offline, and human-in-the-loop evaluations.
Measure workflow time, error costs, calibration, accessibility, adoption barriers, and unintended effects.
Write a deployment decision record with monitoring, rollback, and ownership.

modules.mentalModel: A research prototype becomes an applied contribution only when its context and limits are demonstrated.
modules.tryIt: Create an evaluation plan for a domain partner that includes technical and human success criteria.
modules.outcome: You can connect a model result to a defensible applied research decision.
modules.evidence: Create an evaluation plan for a domain partner that includes technical and human success criteria.

modules.name: Capstone: Cross-Disciplinary Multimodal Study

objectives.text: Partner with a domain expert or use a documented public workflow and formulate one measurable question.
Build a multimodal baseline, run modality and stakeholder-informed ablations, and report limitations.
Deliver a technical report, domain-facing briefing, data statement, and reproducible artifact.

modules.finalResult: A complete cross-disciplinary study showing scientific, technical, and communication maturity.
modules.evidence: A complete cross-disciplinary study showing scientific, technical, and communication maturity.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can turn domain needs into valid technical research.
completionOutcomes: You can design multimodal experiments that expose the source of a claimed improvement.
You can conduct cross-disciplinary research without flattening domain knowledge.
You can connect a model result to a defensible applied research decision.
A complete cross-disciplinary study showing scientific, technical, and communication maturity.

levels.title: Independent Research and Project Leadership
levels.scope: Move from completing exercises to leading a defensible research program with milestones, collaborators, risks, and a clear contribution.

modules.name: From Literature Gap to Contribution

objectives.text: Map a field's established findings, open problems, competing explanations, and available resources.
Test whether a proposed contribution is novel, feasible, important, and distinguishable from prior work.
Define a minimal publishable question and a sequence of risk-reducing pilot studies.

modules.mentalModel: A contribution is a new, reliable answer to a meaningful question, not just a new implementation.
modules.tryIt: Write a novelty matrix comparing a proposed study with ten closest papers.
modules.outcome: You can turn a literature gap into a bounded contribution with a credible plan.
modules.evidence: Write a novelty matrix comparing a proposed study with ten closest papers.

modules.name: Research Planning and Collaboration

objectives.text: Break a project into hypotheses, work packages, milestones, dependencies, and decision gates.
Assign roles, maintain meeting notes, manage review cycles, and resolve disagreements with evidence.
Track compute, data, ethics, authorship, and schedule risks before they become blockers.

modules.mentalModel: Research leadership makes uncertainty visible early enough for a team to act.
modules.tryIt: Run a weekly research meeting using a decision log, risk register, and next-evidence checklist.
modules.outcome: You can coordinate a research project without losing scientific ownership.
modules.evidence: Run a weekly research meeting using a decision log, risk register, and next-evidence checklist.

modules.name: Scientific Presentation and Mentorship

objectives.text: Explain a contribution to a beginner, peer, domain expert, reviewer, and hiring panel.
Design a talk around question, insight, evidence, limitations, and next experiment.
Give constructive code, paper, and presentation feedback while preserving the author's agency.

modules.mentalModel: If the claim cannot survive a change in audience, it probably has not been understood deeply enough.
modules.tryIt: Deliver the same five-minute result briefing to technical and non-technical listeners and revise it from questions.
modules.outcome: You can communicate evidence and mentor others through a research process.
modules.evidence: Deliver the same five-minute result briefing to technical and non-technical listeners and revise it from questions.

modules.name: Capstone: Independent Study Plan

objectives.text: Produce a six-to-twelve-week study plan with literature, hypotheses, pilot, evaluation, risks, and deliverables.
Complete a pilot that can falsify the main idea before committing to full implementation.
Present a go/no-go decision supported by evidence and a revised project schedule.

modules.finalResult: A leadership-ready research plan that protects time, compute, collaborators, and scientific validity.
modules.evidence: A leadership-ready research plan that protects time, compute, collaborators, and scientific validity.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can lead a scoped research project and make go/no-go decisions.
completionOutcomes: You can turn a literature gap into a bounded contribution with a credible plan.
You can coordinate a research project without losing scientific ownership.
You can communicate evidence and mentor others through a research process.
A leadership-ready research plan that protects time, compute, collaborators, and scientific validity.

levels.title: Thesis-Grade Research Portfolio
levels.scope: Execute one substantial research project from question and ethics review through implementation, evaluation, writing, presentation, and artifact release.

modules.name: Proposal, Ethics and Pilot

objectives.text: Finalize the question, hypotheses, related work, data plan, risk assessment, and success criteria.
Complete required permissions, consent or licensing checks, and a reproducibility plan.
Run a pilot that tests feasibility, data quality, compute needs, and the possibility of a meaningful result.

modules.mentalModel: The pilot is valuable even when it disproves the original plan because it prevents expensive invalid work.
modules.tryIt: Hold a proposal defense with two reviewers and revise the protocol before collecting final evidence.
modules.outcome: You can begin a thesis-grade project with a defensible protocol and explicit decision gates.
modules.evidence: Hold a proposal defense with two reviewers and revise the protocol before collecting final evidence.

modules.name: Implementation and Evidence Collection

objectives.text: Implement the method, baselines, data pipeline, logging, tests, and evaluation scripts as one tracked project.
Run planned experiments before exploratory analyses, then label post-hoc discoveries clearly.
Preserve raw artifacts, configurations, seeds, compute logs, and negative results.

modules.mentalModel: Evidence is only interpretable when its provenance and selection process are visible.
modules.tryIt: Run a complete experiment batch from a clean environment and reconstruct one result from stored artifacts.
modules.outcome: You can execute a large study without losing the link between claims and evidence.
modules.evidence: Run a complete experiment batch from a clean environment and reconstruct one result from stored artifacts.

modules.name: Analysis, Limitations and Reproducibility

objectives.text: Analyze effect sizes, uncertainty, subgroup behavior, robustness, and failure cases.
Separate primary, secondary, exploratory, and unsupported findings.
Package code, environment, data access instructions, model cards, and an artifact checklist.

modules.mentalModel: Limitations are part of the result because they define where the evidence stops.
modules.tryIt: Ask an independent reader to reproduce one table and one figure using only the released artifact.
modules.outcome: You can audit your own conclusions and make a study usable by another researcher.
modules.evidence: Ask an independent reader to reproduce one table and one figure using only the released artifact.

modules.name: Capstone: Thesis or Conference Research Portfolio

objectives.text: Deliver a paper-style manuscript, public or restricted artifact, presentation, and plain-language summary.
Defend the work through a mock committee review covering novelty, methods, evidence, limitations, and future work.
Revise the project after feedback and record the final contribution statement.

modules.finalResult: A thesis-grade portfolio demonstrating independent research from initial question to defensible communication.
modules.evidence: A thesis-grade portfolio demonstrating independent research from initial question to defensible communication.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can own a project from proposal through reproducible results.
completionOutcomes: You can begin a thesis-grade project with a defensible protocol and explicit decision gates.
You can execute a large study without losing the link between claims and evidence.
You can audit your own conclusions and make a study usable by another researcher.
A thesis-grade portfolio demonstrating independent research from initial question to defensible communication.

levels.title: Publication, Defense and Research Career
levels.scope: Convert research evidence into a clear manuscript, survive review and defense, and build the portfolio, interview skill, and professional habits needed for research employment.

modules.name: Manuscript, Figures and Open Science

objectives.text: Write an abstract, introduction, related work, methods, results, limitations, and conclusion around one contribution.
Create accessible figures, uncertainty-aware tables, citations, supplementary material, and a reproducibility checklist.
Select a venue by scope, audience, review model, ethics policy, page limits, and realistic contribution fit.

modules.mentalModel: A paper is a compressed argument whose reader must be able to recover the question, evidence, and limits.
modules.tryIt: Rewrite the project as a six-page paper and ask a reader to summarize its claim without your help.
modules.outcome: You can produce a clear, honest, submission-ready manuscript and artifact package.
modules.evidence: Rewrite the project as a six-page paper and ask a reader to summarize its claim without your help.

modules.name: Peer Review, Rebuttal and Revision

objectives.text: Review a paper for novelty, correctness, evidence, clarity, significance, ethics, and reproducibility.
Respond to reviews with a change table, evidence, clarifications, and respectful boundaries.
Revise claims when evidence is weaker than the original narrative and preserve a decision history.

modules.mentalModel: Peer review is a structured conversation about the strength and limits of evidence.
modules.tryIt: Conduct a mock review and rebuttal round with three reviewers who disagree about the main claim.
modules.outcome: You can improve research through criticism without becoming defensive or overstating results.
modules.evidence: Conduct a mock review and rebuttal round with three reviewers who disagree about the main claim.

modules.name: Thesis Defense, Job Talk and Research Interviews

objectives.text: Defend motivation, novelty, design, results, limitations, and future work under unpredictable questions.
Build a research talk, one-page research statement, academic CV, portfolio, and project walkthrough.
Practice coding, statistics, ML system design, paper discussion, behavioral, and collaboration interviews.

modules.mentalModel: A defense or interview tests reasoning under uncertainty, not memorization of every fact.
modules.tryIt: Record a twenty-minute job talk and complete a mock interview using follow-up questions and a structured rubric.
modules.outcome: You can explain your research, solve unfamiliar problems, and show how you work with others.
modules.evidence: Record a twenty-minute job talk and complete a mock interview using follow-up questions and a structured rubric.

modules.name: Career Strategy, Mentorship and Long-Term Growth

objectives.text: Compare research assistant, data scientist, ML engineer, PhD, postdoctoral, and research scientist pathways.
Build a targeted application list, networking message, reference plan, and portfolio evidence for each path.
Set a twelve-month learning and publication plan with feedback, health, ethics, and sustainable work practices.

modules.mentalModel: A research career is a sequence of credible collaborations and questions, not a single title or publication count.
modules.tryIt: Create three role-specific application packets and request feedback from a mentor or experienced researcher.
modules.outcome: You can choose a next step and present evidence that you are ready to grow into it.
modules.evidence: Create three role-specific application packets and request feedback from a mentor or experienced researcher.

modules.name: Capstone: Research Scientist Launch Portfolio

objectives.text: Submit the final manuscript or thesis package, artifact documentation, defense slides, and research statement.
Complete a recorded defense and a full research interview loop, then revise from the rubric.
Publish a personal roadmap naming the next question, collaborators, skills, and evidence you will pursue.

modules.finalResult: A complete research scientist portfolio connecting foundational learning, data science practice, independent evidence, publication, defense, and employment.
modules.evidence: A complete research scientist portfolio connecting foundational learning, data science practice, independent evidence, publication, defense, and employment.

levels.assessmentStandard: Complete the objectives, submit the evidence artifact, and defend the capstone result with limitations.
levels.careerSignal: Can communicate research to reviewers, committees, and employers.
completionOutcomes: You can produce a clear, honest, submission-ready manuscript and artifact package.
You can improve research through criticism without becoming defensive or overstating results.
You can explain your research, solve unfamiliar problems, and show how you work with others.
You can choose a next step and present evidence that you are ready to grow into it.
A complete research scientist portfolio connecting foundational learning, data science practice, independent evidence, publication, defense, and employment.
